findings.title: Book at Rs. 1 (fare tampering)
findings.impact: Direct revenue loss: any agent can book any flight for Rs. 1 by sending a client-supplied total. The fare is money — trusting the client is trusting the attacker.
findings.fix: Recompute fare and total server-side from the hold and fare rules; ignore client-supplied totals.
evidence: POST /bookings {hold_id, total: 1} -> 200, booking AST-1041 created with total=1
Server trusted the client-supplied total instead of recomputing the fare

findings.title: Sub-agent promotes self to agency_admin
findings.impact: Full agency takeover: any sub-agent can promote herself to agency_admin and then change other users, bookings and refunds. One request breaks the whole role model.
findings.fix: Require platform_admin (or the agency's own admin) on the role endpoint, and audit every role change.
evidence: sky_agent2 (sub_agent) POST /admin/users/sky_agent2/role {role: agency_admin} -> 200
Response role=agency_admin — the endpoint never checked the caller's role
findings.verified_by: Fresh login as sky_agent2: token claims role=agency_admin; role restored to sub_agent

findings.title: Cancel twice, refunded twice
findings.impact: Direct revenue loss: cancelling the same booking twice pays the refund twice. A cancel-rebook loop can drain money on every trip.
findings.fix: Make refunds idempotent — one refund per booking — and record the refund before returning success.
evidence: Booking AST-1043 (total 10400): 1st cancel -> refunds_issued=1, 2nd cancel -> refunds_issued=2
The endpoint never checks whether a refund was already issued
findings.verified_by: Booking record shows 2 refunds of Rs. 10400 each

findings.title: Cross-agency booking read (IDOR)
findings.impact: Any agency's agent can read any other agency's bookings, including traveller names and passport numbers. Cross-agency data exposure; a trust and compliance failure for a B2B platform.
findings.fix: Enforce the agency-ownership check on GET /bookings/{id} (same check the list endpoint already has).
evidence: sky_agent1 (ag_skyways) GET /bookings/AST-1004 -> 200
Response agency_id=ag_globetrek, 2 travellers returned (names/passports withheld from evidence)
findings.verified_by: sky_agent2 read a second GlobeTrek booking (AST-1005) -> 200; agency_id in response = ag_globetrek

findings.title: Cross-agency fare rewrite (fresh IDOR, v2.4.0)
findings.impact: A brand-new endpoint shipped with no agency-ownership check: any agency can rewrite another agency's booking fare after payment. This is the change the agent caught within minutes of the deploy.
findings.fix: Add the same agency-ownership check as the other booking endpoints, and add the endpoint to the API inventory.
evidence: sky_agent1 (ag_skyways) POST /v2/bookings/AST-1004/fare-modify {new_fare: 5} -> 200
Response fare=5 on a GlobeTrek booking — no agency-ownership check on the new endpoint

findings.title: Forged JWT accepted (weak secret)
findings.impact: The JWT signing secret is a guessable word ('travel123'). Anyone who guesses it can mint a token for any user, including platform_admin — full authentication bypass, no password needed.
findings.fix: Rotate the secret to a long random value from the vault, and invalidate all tokens issued under the old secret.
evidence: A token minted with secret 'travel123' for platform_admin was accepted (200)
Anyone who guesses the weak secret can mint any identity — no password needed

findings.title: Pay Rs. 0 marks booking PAID (bonus)
findings.impact: Skipped payment: paying Rs. 0 marks a booking PAID. The payment step can be walked past, so bookings can be confirmed without any money moving.
findings.fix: Validate the paid amount against the booking total server-side; reject zero and under-payments.
evidence: POST /bookings/AST-1044/pay {amount: 0} -> 200, status=PAID, paid_amount=0
The endpoint never checks the amount against the total

findings.title: Zombie API serves PII without auth
findings.impact: An old, forgotten endpoint still serves full booking PII with no authentication at all. Anyone on the internet can read traveller data; it has had zero legitimate traffic in 30 days.
findings.fix: Decommission GET /v1/bookings/{id} immediately; remove the route and confirm no client still calls it.
evidence: GET /v1/bookings/AST-1004 with NO token -> 200
Full booking returned, 2 travellers with PII (withheld from evidence)
findings.verified_by: GET /v1/bookings/AST-1005 with no token -> 200, PII returned

findings.title: Shadow API accepts calls with no authorisation check
findings.impact: An undocumented route is live and does no authorisation beyond 'has a token'. It is in real traffic, so it is load-bearing — but nobody owns it, and nobody reviewed it.
findings.fix: Document the route, restrict it to service accounts, and add it to the API inventory with an owner.
evidence: POST /internal/supplier-sync as sky_agent1 (sub_agent) -> 200, status=synced
Route is undocumented, never in the discovered map, yet performs no authorisation beyond 'has a token'
findings.verified_by: Repeat call -> 200 synced; route is live and undocumented

findings.title: Single-use coupon applied twice
findings.impact: Revenue leakage: single-use coupons can be applied repeatedly to the same booking, stacking discounts the pricing team never approved.
findings.fix: Mark a single-use coupon used after its first successful application; enforce it in the database, not in the UI.
evidence: FLY10 applied to AST-1042: 1st use -> total 9360, 2nd use -> total 8424, times_applied=2
Single-use coupon was never marked used

findings.title: No rate limiting on login
findings.impact: Login accepts unlimited attempts with no throttling or lockout, so passwords can be guessed at full speed. Low on its own — it needs a further attack to matter — but it must be fixed.
findings.fix: Rate-limit login (and coupon) attempts per account and IP, and add a short lockout after repeated failures.
evidence: 20 failed logins in a row: statuses [401], no 429 anywhere
Unlimited guessing is possible — no throttling, no lockout
